change.title: Include the identity event in the Birmingham process
change.reason: Make event.identity the first milestone of process.birmingham_estate, preceding funeral and inheritance actions. The event occurs within the process on 2 January 1972 and already has no category, so it inherits the process category. Approval covers the complete resulting process record.

before.title: Birmingham, an accident and its aftermath
before.description: Operating as Adam Pleskot, Vincent spends 2 January to 2 February 1972 in Birmingham arranging the parents’ funeral, settling inheritance formalities and disposing of the family estate. After expenses he holds approximately GBP 6,000 and his remaining belongings for departure.

participant.role: protagonist; Vincent operating as Adam Pleskot after the identity takeover

inputs.description: The parents’ deaths and Vincent’s assumption of Adam’s identity create the need and opportunity to settle family affairs.
The estate includes the Birmingham house and saleable possessions, together with an insurance claim for the single family car destroyed in the fatal accident.

steps.description: Handle the formalities connected with inheriting the parents’ wealth.

Sell the house and saleable possessions, settle the insurance claim for the destroyed family car and receive its payout, handle any salvage formalities, and settle estate and funeral expenses. Retain approximately GBP 6,000 net and the remaining belongings for departure.

outcomes.description: The parents’ funeral has been arranged and inheritance formalities handled.

Adam holds approximately GBP 6,000 in net estate proceeds, including the crashed car’s insurance payout, and his remaining belongings after disposal and expenses. The car is not sold as a usable vehicle. The insurance amount is unspecified and is included in, rather than added to, the GBP 6,000 total.
